messages: If you are budgeting for a shot blasting project, you have probably noticed that most contractors are reluctant to publish prices online. That is because the cost of shot blasting varies significantly depending on the size of the job, the substrate condition, the type of media used, and the location. This guide breaks down the real cost drivers and gives you realistic price ranges so you can plan your budget with confidence.
## What Affects the Cost of Shot Blasting?
### Surface Area and Accessibility

The single biggest cost driver is the total surface area to be treated, measured in square metres. A straightforward flat steel floor or a large structural beam is quick to blast; a complex fabrication with tight angles, bolt holes, and internal cavities takes considerably longer per square metre. Scaffolding or elevated access equipment adds further cost.
### Substrate Condition

Steel that has been sitting outside for years, covered in heavy mill scale, thick rust, or multiple layers of old paint, requires more passes and more abrasive media than a lightly contaminated surface. Contractors will typically assess the initial surface preparation grade (Sa 1 to Sa 3 under ISO 8501-1) and price accordingly.
### Cleanliness Standard Required

The target cleanliness standard has a direct impact on cost. Sa 2 (thorough blast cleaning) is faster and cheaper than Sa 2.5 (very thorough blast cleaning) or Sa 3 (blast cleaning to visually clean steel). For most structural steel and industrial applications, Sa 2.5 is the minimum specified by coating manufacturers. [Intumescent painting](/services/intumescent-painting) and high-performance epoxy coatings typically require Sa 2.5 or Sa 3.
### Profile Depth

Coating specifications often require a specific anchor profile depth, measured in microns. Achieving a deeper profile (e.g. 75–100 µm for heavy-duty coatings) requires harder or larger media and more energy, which increases cost compared to a standard 40–60 µm profile.
### Location and Mobilisation

Shot blasting is a mobile service. For projects in [Staffordshire](/counties/staffordshire), the [West Midlands](/counties/west-midlands), and surrounding counties, mobilisation costs are minimal. For remote sites in [Cumbria](/counties/cumbria), [Northumberland](/counties/northumberland), or [Cornwall](/counties/cornwall), travel time and fuel add to the overall price. Always ask whether the quoted price includes mobilisation or whether it is charged separately.
### Volume and Repeat Business
Like most trade services, shot blasting is cheaper per square metre at scale. A one-off 50 m² job will cost more per m² than a 500 m² project or a rolling contract covering multiple sites.
## Typical Shot Blasting Price Ranges

The terms "shot blasting" and "sandblasting" are often used interchangeably by clients, but they describe different processes that produce different results on different substrates. Choosing the wrong method can lead to inadequate surface preparation, coating failure, or unnecessary cost. This article explains the key differences so you can specify the right process for your project.
## What Is Sandblasting?

Sandblasting — more accurately called abrasive blasting or grit blasting — is a surface preparation process in which abrasive particles are propelled at high velocity against a surface using compressed air. The abrasive strips rust, mill scale, paint, and other contaminants from the substrate and creates a mechanical anchor profile for subsequent coatings.

Historically, the abrasive used was silica sand. However, silica sand has been banned for use in blasting operations in the UK and across the EU since 1966 under the Blasting (Castings and Other Articles) Special Regulations, because fine silica dust causes silicosis — a fatal and irreversible lung disease. Modern abrasive blasting operations use alternative media such as steel grit, aluminium oxide, garnet, or recycled glass. The term "sandblasting" has persisted in common usage despite the ban, which is why you will still hear it used to describe what is technically abrasive grit blasting.
## What Is Shot Blasting?

Shot blasting is a specific form of abrasive blasting in which the abrasive is propelled by a centrifugal wheel rather than compressed air. Steel shot or steel grit is fed into a spinning impeller wheel that accelerates the particles to high velocity and directs them at the workpiece. The process is typically carried out in an enclosed blast cabinet or blast room, or using a self-contained mobile blast unit for on-site work.

The key distinction is the propulsion method: compressed air (abrasive blasting / "sandblasting") versus centrifugal wheel (shot blasting). Both methods achieve similar surface cleanliness standards, but they differ in efficiency, cost, and the type of profile they produce.
## Key Differences at a Glance
| Factor | Shot Blasting (Wheel) | Abrasive/Grit Blasting (Air) |
| Propulsion method | Centrifugal wheel | Compressed air |
| Production rate | Very high (up to 30 m²/hr) | Moderate (3–10 m²/hr) |
| Media consumption | Low (closed-loop recycling) | Higher (open-loop or partial recovery) |
| Profile type | Rounded (shot) or angular (grit) | Angular |
| Dust generation | Low (enclosed process) | Higher (open process) |
| Portability | Limited (requires blast room or mobile unit) | High (can access any geometry) |
| Best suited for | Flat or regular surfaces, high volume | Complex shapes, on-site work, spot repairs |
## Which Method Is Right for Your Project?

When structural steel is specified for a construction project in the UK, the surface preparation standard is not left to the contractor's discretion. It is defined in the project specification, referenced to an international standard, and verified by inspection before coating is applied. Understanding these standards — and ensuring your shot blasting contractor can meet them — is essential for any engineer, specifier, or project manager working with structural steel.
## The Key Standards
### ISO 8501-1: Visual Assessment of Surface Cleanliness
ISO 8501-1 is the primary standard for assessing the cleanliness of steel surfaces before coating. It defines four blast cleaning grades:
| Grade | Description |
| Sa 1 | Light blast cleaning — loose mill scale, rust, and coatings removed |
| Sa 2 | Thorough blast cleaning — most mill scale, rust, and coatings removed |
| Sa 2.5 | Very thorough blast cleaning — residual staining limited to 5% of surface |
| Sa 3 | Blast cleaning to visually clean steel — no visible contamination |

Sa 2.5 is the minimum grade specified for the vast majority of structural steel coating systems in the UK. Sa 3 is required for high-performance systems such as [intumescent fire protection coatings](/services/intumescent-painting) and immersion-service coatings. Our [structural steel shot blasting](/services/structural-steel-shot-blasting) service routinely achieves Sa 2.5 and Sa 3 to order.
### ISO 8503: Surface Roughness (Profile)

ISO 8503 defines the anchor profile of a blast-cleaned surface, measured using comparator discs or replica tape. The profile is expressed in microns (µm) and classified as Fine, Medium, or Coarse. Most structural steel coating specifications require a Medium profile of 40–70 µm, though some high-build systems require a Coarse profile of 70–100 µm.

The profile is created by the abrasive media. Steel grit produces a sharp, angular profile suitable for most coating systems. Steel shot produces a rounded, peened profile more suited to fatigue-improvement applications. For structural steel preparation, steel grit or a grit/shot mix is standard.
### ISO 8502: Tests for the Assessment of Surface Cleanliness
Before coating is applied, the prepared surface must be assessed for:
- **Soluble salt contamination** (Bresle patch test, ISO 8502-6/9) — salt residues cause osmotic blistering under coatings and must be below the threshold specified in the coating system data sheet.
- **Dust** (tape test, ISO 8502-3) — dust from blasting must be removed before coating.
- **Oil and grease** — any contamination must be removed by solvent cleaning before blasting.
A competent shot blasting contractor will carry out these assessments as a matter of course and provide documentation to support your quality records.
